name: Grape
grown_as: Grape vines on wires, a wall or under glass. William grows 'Pinot Noir', 'Cardinal', 'Red Globe', 'Boskoop Glory' and 'Venus' ('Venus' and 'Boskoop Glory' are hybrids with American vines, which look much the same). Most have black or red fruit; the drawing shows black grapes.
habit: A woody climbing vine, pruned to a short framework of trunk and rods, 2 to 3 m on wires (unpruned 10 m or more). Old bark brown and shaggy, peeling in long strips. Climbs by forked tendrils, each standing opposite a leaf.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, with a tendril or a flower cluster opposite most leaves
leaf.outline: Roundish, 10 to 20 cm across, with three to five lobes (shallow to deep by variety)
leaf.base: Deeply heart-shaped, with a narrow notch where the stalk joins
leaf.margin: Coarse, sharp, irregular teeth all round
leaf.veins: Five main veins from the top of the stalk, one into each lobe, with straight side veins running into the teeth
leaf.surface: Smooth mid green above; paler beneath, smooth or with cobweb-like hairs
leaf.colour: Mid green; yellow, or red in black-fruited varieties, in autumn

flower.form: A tiny flower whose petals never open: they stay joined at the tips and fall off together as a little cap
flower.petals: Five, green, joined at the tips into a cap that drops at flowering
flower.centre: Five stamens with yellow anthers spreading out round a small green ovary
flower.behind: A tiny green rim of sepals
flower.carried: Many together in dense, branched, cone-shaped clusters (panicles) 5 to 15 cm long, opposite the leaves, upright at first then hanging

fruit: Round to oval berries, 1 to 2.5 cm, in hanging cone-shaped bunches 10 to 25 cm long. Green and hard at first, then (in black varieties) turning blue-black to purple with a pale bloom; 'Red Globe' and 'Cardinal' ripen red. September to October.
seedling: Not drawn: grown as bought plants
winter: Bare, pruned framework: a gnarled trunk with shaggy peeling bark and short spurs or one or two long brown rods along a wire, each with buds at the nodes.

leaf: roundish leaf with three to five pointed lobes
deeply heart-shaped base with a narrow notch at the stalk
five main veins from the stalk
bloom: a tiny green flower with stamens spread out and the petal cap lifting off
part of a dense branched cluster
young: a single woody stem on a support
lobed leaves with tendrils opposite them
dormant: a bare pruned framework with peeling bark on wires
flower: dense green flower clusters opposite the leaves
crop: hanging cone-shaped bunches of round dark blue-black grapes with a bloom

look_alikes: Virginia creeper has leaves of five separate leaflets. Hop leaves are rough and opposite, and the plant twines without tendrils. Ornamental vines (Vitis coignetiae) have huge, barely lobed leaves.
